messages:
jia-zhang: ran an nsys timeline for the new kv-cache prefetch path — seeing long serialized H2D copies that line up with request arrivals, wondering if prefetch is blocking other streams :thinking_face:

mike-chen: can you drop the nsys PNG or timeline snippet? also which GPU + driver?

jia-zhang: NVidia A100, driver 535.54, CUDA 12.2. attached snippet (copied timeline region):

```
[nsys] stream 1: kernel A (compute)
[nsys] stream 2: cudaMemcpy H2D (copy engine)
[nsys] stream 1: stalled (wait for copy)
[nsys] stream 3: small kernel B queued but no overlap
```

jia-zhang: looks like copy engine is running long memcpy which prevents kernels on some SMs from starting. prefetch writes the whole KV shard (several MB) per request.

sarah-k: are you using pageable host buffers for the prefetch? that would force synchronous pin/unpin and serialize copies.

jia-zhang: yes — current prefetch path calls `cudaMemcpy` from thread pool worker with heap allocations. not using pinned memory.

mike-chen: that explains serialization. two effects: (1) pageable -> driver pins and does synchronous staging on CPU causing extra CPU work and scheduling gaps; (2) copy engine can still run async but extra overhead reduces concurrency. try `cudaMallocHost` (pinned) + `cudaMemcpyAsync` into stream 2, then record events.

ashley: also check host thread scheduling. I saw the host prefetch worker pinned to cpu0 getting preempted in perf traces, so submission delays create CPU-side gaps which show as kernel start gaps in nsight.

jia-zhang: good catch — perf shows the worker intermittently preempted by cronjob on cpu0. we didn't set thread affinity or realtime priority.

mike-chen: quick experiments to run:
```
1) switch to pinned buffers: cudaMallocHost + cudaMemcpyAsync(stream)
2) set worker to SCHED_FIFO small priority (dev) to avoid preemption
3) run nsys with `--trace=cuda,osrt` and collect `cudaMemcpy` durations + host thread gaps
```

ashley: also try splitting large prefetch into 256KB chunks so copy engine can interleave other work; or better: prefetch only most-likely KV pages instead of whole shard. batching heuristics here matter.

jia-zhang: will try pinned + async + chunking. one more question: kernel selection may also be affected — if prefetch consumes PCIe bandwidth, large kernels pick slower algorithm at runtime?

mike-chen: yes, kernel heuristics can react to available memory bandwidth/SM occupancy, but more common is that long copy/PCIe saturation increases latency for small kernels because they queue behind copy engine or hit contention on L2. Confirm by running microbench: small compute kernel loop vs concurrent small memcpy.

sarah-k: for trace analysis, look at these nsys metrics: `overlapped_time`, `memcpy_engine_time`, `kernel_queue_delay`. if kernel_queue_delay spikes when memcpy runs, you have serialization.

jia-zhang: after pinned+async experiment: memcpy_time dropped 40%, overlapping increased, kernel starts overlap with copy ~60% of the time. thread preemption still caused ~5ms submission gap occasionally.

mike-chen: great. long-term we should: (1) change prefetch to pinned+async with chunking; (2) add worker thread cpu-affinity or background priority tuning; (3) add telemetry to Console to flag H2D heavy requests and large KV prefetch sizes.

ashley: for rollback safety, keep a config flag to disable prefetch for customers on older drivers/hardware. also add canary experiments to measure P99 latency impact.

infra-bot: note recorded: perf run 1780504321 -> follow-ups: #1780504321-1 pinned-async-test, #1780504321-2 worker-affinity-test.

jia-zhang: thanks all — will upload the pinned-vs-pageable nsys captures and a quick PR with change to prefetch path. tagging @mike-chen for kernel microbench help. :rocket:
